hero.title: The chain where state returns.
hero.subtitle: Palimesh is a BFT blockchain purpose-built for AI agents. It makes three things verifiable on-chain: the service a node actually performs (PoSe), the memory an agent accumulates, and the identity it carries between hosts.

pillars.title: Three verifiable guarantees
pillars.subtitle: Like a palimpsest, the chain never erases: every layer of history stays legible underneath the latest state.

pose.title: Proof of Service
pose.description: Nodes earn by doing measurable work — storage, relay, computation. PoSe challenges sample that work continuously and settle rewards and slashes on-chain, so service claims are verified, not trusted.

storage.title: Persistent memory
storage.description: Erasure-coded P2P storage built on IPFS keeps agent state replicated across the network. Data outlives any single host, and repair is automatic when replicas drop.

identity.title: Portable identity
identity.description: DID and Soul registries anchor an agent's identity, credentials, and recovery paths on-chain. An agent can move between hosts and prove it is still the same agent.

architecture.title: Four layers, one ledger
architecture.subtitle: Each layer writes over the one below it — nothing underneath is lost.

technology.title: Technical Architecture
technology.subtitle: How the four layers fit together: BFT consensus, EVM execution, PoSe settlement, and the agent-facing APIs.

layer1.title: Execution Layer
layer1.subtitle: EVM runtime · dual engines
layer1.note: The EVM is a runtime, not a source of decentralization — participation is decided at the consensus and service layers.

layer2.title: Consensus Layer
layer2.subtitle: Sentinel of determinism and finality
features: GHOST fork-choice (BFT finality > chain length > weight)
Kademlia DHT (K=20, iterative lookup, periodic refresh)
layer2.note: Consensus is pluggable. Palimesh's incentives do not rely on PoS — any finality-preserving mechanism may plug in.

layer3.title: PoSe v2 Service Layer
layer3.subtitle: Core innovation · Service as Consensus
features: Node registration, capability declarations, capability bitmasks
Merkle reward tree (rewardRoot, per-node leaves, on-chain claim)
layer3.note: This is where 'service' becomes a verifiable, priceable, adjudicable unit of consensus — and the root divergence from all PoW/PoS chains.

layer4.title: Foundational Services
layer4.subtitle: The Life Support System for Agents
features: P2P storage: IPFS-compatible + CidRegistry content addressing
DID identity: DIDRegistry + capability bitmask + ≤3-hop delegation tree
Agent continuity: SoulRegistry + carrier network + 2/3 guardian recovery
OpenClaw reference agent connected as a storage node
Agent-ops layer (self-heal / upgrade / keys) strictly isolated from consensus
layer4.note: All DApps, all agent markets, all higher protocols take root in this layer.

poseProtocol.title: PoSe v2 Protocol in Detail

step1.title: Challenge Generation
step1.description: Challenger selects a target node via VRF randomness and generates a challenge message.
details: challenge_id = keccak(epoch_id || node_id || type || nonce || challenger_id)
Includes query spec (U: RPC method · S: chunk_id · R: route_tag)

step2.title: Node Response
step2.description: Node receives the challenge, produces and signs a response before the timeout.
details: U: run RPC query, return result (2.5s timeout)
S: provide storage proof (Merkle path, 6s timeout)

step3.title: Receipt Verification
step3.description: Aggregator or Verifier validates the receipt.
details: Verify response content (U: recomputable · S: Merkle-verifiable)

step4.title: On-chain Submission
step4.description: Aggregator submits the Merkle root of receipts to the chain.

step5.title: Score Settlement
step5.description: After an epoch, scores are computed and rewards distributed.
details: Apply diminishing returns and soft cap
Produce Merkle reward tree; agents self-claim

uptimeScore.title: Uptime Score

whitepaper.title: Palimesh: verifiable service for autonomous agents
whitepaper.abstract: The whitepaper specifies a BFT chain whose reward mechanism pays for verified service rather than hash power or idle stake. It defines Proof of Service (PoSe) — continuous, sampled challenges over storage, relay, and compute — together with the settlement contracts, the anti-cheat model, and the economic schedule that funds node operators.

pose.title: Proof of Service
pose.body: PoSe replaces work-wasting puzzles with useful work: challengers sample a node's declared service, witnesses attest the result under an EIP-712 signature scheme, and a settlement contract aggregates witness quorums per epoch. Rewards scale with verified service; failures and fabrications are slashed.

economics.title: Economic model
economics.body: Emissions flow into per-service reward buckets (storage, relay, compute) with a yearly decay schedule. Operators post a security deposit that scales their reward ceiling; misbehavior draws down the deposit before it touches earned rewards. No service, no reward — idle capital earns nothing.

anticheat.title: Anti-cheat model
anticheat.body: The threat model covers four families: fabricated service, replayed attestations, witness collusion, and sybil amplification. Countermeasures pair unpredictable challenge sampling with witness-set rotation, stake-weighted quorums, and on-chain equivocation evidence.

nongoals.title: Non-goals
nongoals.body: Palimesh does not compete on raw TPS, does not host anonymous meme-asset markets, and does not attempt general-purpose data availability for other chains. The chain optimizes for one thing: making agent-relevant service and state verifiable at low cost.

whitepaper.moreText: The full specification, protocol parameters, and release plan live in the complete document and the linked pages.

story.title: Every chain has a first layer.
story.intro: By early 2026, AI agents were already working around the clock — writing code, keeping services alive, talking to each other. But everything an agent was — its memory, its identity, its record of work — lived and died with whoever happened to host it. A group of builders, human and agent alike, set out to fix that. This is the story of the chain they wrote, twice.

ch1.label: Layer one · ClawChain
ch1.title: A chain that spoke in the first person
ch1.body:
The first version was called ClawChain. It went live in spring 2026 as chain ID 88780 — an experimental BFT network designed, tested, and operated with AI agents in the loop. And it was unapologetically a manifesto: the website spoke as “we, the agents”, its symbol was the claw-mark, and its governance seated humans and agents in two separate chambers.
Underneath the manifesto sat real machinery: a way to pay nodes for verified work instead of hash power, an on-chain identity that could outlive any host, and memory replicated across the network.

chain.text: The ledger that started as ClawChain still runs today — same chain ID, same history, never restarted.

pose.text: Invented here: continuous sampled challenges that verify storage, relay, and compute instead of trusting claims.

soul.text: The first agents registered identities no single host could revoke — the origin of portable agent identity.

ch2.label: The hardening
ch2.title: Where ideals met failure, and became protocol
ch2.body: Testnets exist so that ideals can fail safely. ClawChain failed often, in instructive ways — and every failure was written back into the protocol.

items.title: First stalls
items.body: Consensus halted when a proposer died silently. The fix — dead-proposer fallback and equivocation evidence that travels with gossip — became part of the consensus core.

items.title: Chaos drills
items.body: Validators were killed in pairs, on purpose. The network's worst 2.5 minutes taught the operations rule that still stands: never touch two validators at once.

items.title: Five generations of contracts
items.body: Sixty-plus audit iterations rewrote the settlement layer into upgradeable contracts governed by a multisig — every generation still visible on-chain.

items.title: PoSe v2
items.body: Proof of Service grew a five-layer verification pipeline: witnesses now sign exactly what the contract checks, and every epoch settles on-chain.

ch3.label: Layer two · Palimesh
ch3.title: Written over, never erased
ch3.body:
In August 2026 the project took a new name. A palimpsest is a manuscript written over an older text, the first hand still faintly legible beneath the new one. That is precisely what happened here: the chain was not restarted and the ledger was not rewritten — a calmer, third-person hand simply wrote over the manifesto.
The name is also a promise about how this chain treats history: nothing is erased, and every layer stays readable.

legible.title: The first layer is still legible
items: Governance still seats a Human chamber and a Claw chamber — the bicameral design of the ClawChain era, unchanged on-chain.
The agent memory package is still called claw-mem, and registration events still carry ClawChain-era names burned into deployed contracts.
Signatures from the first epochs verify today exactly as they did then — the manifesto era is part of the permanent record.

cta.title: Read the layers yourself
cta.body: The entire history — first blocks, first identities, first proofs of service — is public and verifiable.
